loopIdea: The closing beat is the same ground-level tracking shot of the same front tire rolling beside the same painted lane line, now running parallel instead of drifting off it, so a replay picks up mid-roll as the line slides away again.
mechanicTruth: When a pull shows up tells you where it comes from: a pull that appears only while braking points at the brakes, because that is the only time the brake system is loaded, while a pull that is there all the time points at alignment or uneven tire pressure, which act on the car whether or not you are on the pedal.
selectedCaption: The wheel is straight. The car isn't. A pull has more than one cause, and they're not equally urgent. Only pulls when you brake? That can point to the brakes. Pulls all the time? That can point to alignment - or just uneven tire pressure. Check pressure first. It costs nothing, and it's often the answer. Worth checking before it becomes a bigger fix.
voiceoverScript: The wheel's straight. The car isn't. Only when braking? Brakes. All the time? Alignment or pressure. Check pressure first; soft tires mimic both. The pattern tells you.
